messages:

Subject: Dedicated capacity — hybrid commit question

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our infra and procurement teams: we like the idea of reserving capacity per-region but we have seasonal spikes where APAC and EU will need to burst into US pools for 2–6 hour windows.

Questions: would Redwood support a hybrid commit where we have reserved minimum pools in EU/APAC and a shared US pool we can burst into with pre-negotiated credits? Also: what are the throughput guarantees by pool, and can we get headroom credits for DR drills?

Procurement will also need a rough TCV and an outline of how credits/overage are billed so we can model cost for our Q4 ramp. Attached is a sample traffic profile.

Can you loop in pricing/solutions so we get something concrete in the next week?

Best,
Sanjay
VP of Platforms — Acme AI

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — hybrid commit question

Hi Sanjay — great working through this with you.

Short answers up front: yes, we can structure a hybrid commit that combines per-region reserved pools (EU/APAC minimums) with a cross-region shared bursting pool in US for short windows.

High-level mechanics we'll propose:
- Reserved minimums per region: guaranteed GPU quantity and baseline throughput SLA (tokens/sec aggregate per pool).
- Cross-region bursting: pre-authorized credit bucket that can be consumed when traffic exceeds regional reserved capacity; billing against committed credits first, then overage rate.
- DR drills / headroom credits: we can include an annual allotment of DR credits for failover testing (non-production drills) that do not count toward overage if used within agreed windows.

I'll loop in Ben (solutions) and Marissa (dedicated packaging) to scope exact GPU sizing and discounts. Can you confirm target steady-state qps and maximum 95th-percentile peak duration? That will let us size the shared pool and propose a credit bucket.

I'll follow up with a draft term sheet and a cost model later today.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Acme hybrid commit — quick internal alignment (sizing + discount asks)

Team — forwarding Acme's profile and initial ask. Key asks: separate minimum pools in EU/APAC; shared US bursting pool; headroom credits for DR drills; they want TCV for Q4 ramp.

Notes / proposed approach:
1) Sizing: based on their attached CSV, I estimate ~60 steady GPUs across EU/APAC combined for baseline (split 35 EU / 25 APAC), with a 15–20 GPU shared US burst pool for 3–6 hr windows at 95th p95 traffic. Ben — can you validate if continuous batching + kv-cache will change GPU count assumptions?
2) Billing mechanics: propose a two-layer commit: 1) regional reserved (monthly commit, smaller discount tier) + 2) cross-region bursting credits purchased up-front at a higher per-credit discount if they commit to 12 months. Credits consume first. Overage billed hourly at a premium.
3) DR headroom: offer 120 DR credits/year (counts as credit bucket separate from bursting) for smoke tests <2 hrs without overage billing.
4) Discounts: sliding scale — 10% off list for 6m commit, 18% for 12m, add-on 3% for multi-region commit if they lock EU+APAC+US baseline. Avoiding large up-front TCV asks but keep multi-year levers.

Marissa — can you model 3 variants (conservative, expected, aggressive) with GPU counts and monthly TCVs? Ben/Karthik — note potential to reduce GPU need via quantization suggestion in the conservative plan; also confirm any cross-region egress or replication fees if we enable active-active replication.

I want a draft pricing PDF by EOD so we can share with Sanjay tomorrow.

Thanks,
Rachel

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 31 Jul 2025 08:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme hybrid commit — quick internal alignment (sizing + discount asks)

Rachel / team — ran a quick pass on the traffic CSV and assumptions. Quick findings:

- With continuous batching and prefix caching we can compress their 95th-percentile peak profile by ~18–22% token-wise, which reduces required GPUs in the shared burst pool from 15–20 to ~12–16 depending on model selection and sequence-length distribution.
- If they opt for a single-architecture quantized variant for burst traffic (faster kernels), we can reduce burst GPU count further ~2 GPUs but that requires model onboarding + verification (2–3 week pipeline).
- Active-active replication across regions will incur a replication premium: approx 6% on top of committed pool fees (covers cross-region state sync + persistent KV replication). Active-passive (hot-standby) drops that premium but increases failover time SLAs.

Pricing mechanics / recommended packaging:
A) Option A — Minimal risk (conservative):
  - EU reserved: 35 GPUs (monthly commit)
  - APAC reserved: 25 GPUs (monthly commit)
  - US shared burst: 12 GPUs (credit bucket)
  - Annual DR credits: 120
  - Discount: 12% on committed regional pools, credits priced at committed discount + 2% premium

B) Option B — Balanced (expected):
  - EU: 30 GPUs
  - APAC: 20 GPUs
  - US burst: 16 GPUs
  - DR credits: 120 (included)
  - Discount: 16% on regional commit, credits deeper discount if 12m commit
  - Active-passive replication included; active-active add-on +6%

C) Option C — Aggressive commit (best price):
  - EU: 25 GPUs
  - APAC: 20 GPUs
  - US burst: 20 GPUs (bigger shared pool)
  - DR credits: 180
  - Discount: 20% on committed pools + 3% multi-region bonus
  - Requires 12-month minimum; includes 1 DR failover drill per quarter

Action items: Marissa — please convert these into a one-page pricing summary + TCV table (monthly and annualized) and a short footnote on replication premiums and egress assumptions. Rachel — I can join the call with Sanjay tomorrow to walk through tradeoffs.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
